theme: 3 terms on access control: hiding code inside a type, sharing it inside your module, and opening it to other modules

terms.definition: A keyword that hides a property or method from all code outside its own type.
terms.example: I made `cash` Private, so only `Wallet` can read it.

terms.definition: A keyword for the default level that lets any code in your own module use a type, but hides it from other modules.
terms.example: `Tab` is Internal by default, so the whole app can use it.

terms.definition: A keyword that lets code in other modules use a type or member, as long as it is marked with it.
terms.example: I made `Badge` Public so the other framework can use it.

quizzes.question: What do you call the default level that your whole module can use, but other modules cannot?
What lets code in other modules use a type, once you mark it?

video.title: Private, Internal & Public in Swift | Day 34
video.description:
Learn to explain who can see your code in Swift: Private, Internal & Public, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Private - A keyword that hides a property or method from all code outside its own type.
Internal - A keyword for the default level that lets any code in your own module use a type, but hides it from other modules.
Public - A keyword that lets code in other modules use a type or member, as long as it is marked with it.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Private, Internal & Public Access Control | Day 34
landscape.description:
Explain Private, Internal & Public in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
프라이빗, 인터널, 퍼블릭 접근 수준 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Private - A keyword that hides a property or method from all code outside its own type.
한국어: 프라이빗: 자기 타입 바깥의 모든 코드에서 프로퍼티나 메서드를 숨기는 키워드

Internal - A keyword for the default level that lets any code in your own module use a type, but hides it from other modules.
한국어: 인터널: 같은 모듈 안의 모든 코드는 쓸 수 있고 다른 모듈에는 숨기는 기본 접근 수준 키워드

Public - A keyword that lets code in other modules use a type or member, as long as it is marked with it.
한국어: 퍼블릭: 다른 모듈의 코드도 쓸 수 있게 열어 주는 접근 수준 키워드

In this video, Mina and Jake sort out why a property is hidden, what the default level is and what other modules can see, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain these access levels in English?

dialogue.title: Why is secret hidden?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, why can't I read `secret` from `Badge`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is Private, so only code inside `Badge` can use it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: OK. And `label`? I did not write any keyword there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then it is Internal by default. Your whole app can see it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I make `Badge` Public and everything works?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not everything. Each member needs its own keyword, like `count`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right, `count` is Public, but `label` stays Internal.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Another module can use only the Public parts.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And `secret` stays Private, even inside the app?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Start with Private, then open it up when you need to.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Private first, Internal by default, Public for others.
Keep it Private until another type needs it.
